subject: funder
label: maintains
description: A Funder maintains one or more Grant Programs, each of which issues Funding Opportunities over time.

subject: grant-program
label: issues
description: A Grant Program issues Funding Opportunities during defined Funding Cycles.

subject: funding-opportunity
label: occurs during
description: A Funding Opportunity is issued within a defined Funding Cycle.

subject: funding-opportunity
label: specifies
description: A Funding Opportunity specifies the Eligibility Criteria an applicant must meet.

subject: funding-opportunity
label: may require
description: A Funding Opportunity may require a Letter of Inquiry before a full Application is invited.

subject: grantee
label: submits
description: A Grantee (or a project operating under a Fiscal Sponsor) submits an Application in response to a Funding Opportunity.

subject: application
label: responds to
description: An Application is submitted in response to a specific Funding Opportunity.

subject: application
label: includes
description: An Application includes a proposed Budget.

subject: fiscal-sponsor
label: acts on behalf of
description: A Fiscal Sponsor stands in for a Grantee that lacks independent legal status to receive an Award directly.

subject: organization
label: plays
description: An Organization plays one or more Organization Roles, each a contextual, independently-scoped occupancy rather than a permanent trait.

subject: organization-role
label: applies within
description: An Organization Role is scoped to the Philanthropic Arrangement it was granted within, so the same organization can hold different roles in different arrangements.

subject: organization-role
label: applies within
description: An Organization Role can also be scoped directly to an Organization rather than an Arrangement -- e.g. a Contractor, Vendor, Service Provider, Employer, or Partner role is naturally scoped to which organization it relates to, not to a Philanthropic Arrangement. A distinct predicate from rel-organization-role-applies-within for the same reason Phase 3.7 Milestone 1's Person relationships needed distinct names: the generator requires every relationship predicate to be globally unique, so one predicate can't have two different declared object concepts. Broadening this into a true Role-appliesWithin-Context union (Award, Application, Agreement, Fund, Grant Program, Funding Opportunity, Project, Review, Payment, Decision, per the Phase 3.7 roadmap) is deferred until real worked-example data actually needs one of those specific contexts -- adding all of them speculatively now, each as its own distinct predicate, would be exactly the kind of premature abstraction this project avoids.

subject: organization
label: has legal form
description: An Organization has a legal form describing what it fundamentally is under law, independent of any role it plays.

subject: organization
label: participates in
description: An Organization participates in a Philanthropic Arrangement, independent of tracking which specific role it occupies there.

subject: philanthropic-arrangement
label: is administered by
description: A Philanthropic Arrangement is administered by an Organization, such as a fiscal sponsor or fund administrator.

subject: grant-program
label: is funded by
description: A Grant Program is funded by a Fund -- the pool of financial resources backing the program's giving strategy.

subject: fund
label: is held by
description: A Fund is held and administered by an Organization.

subject: award
label: is funded from
description: An Award draws its funds from a specific Fund.

subject: award
label: is awarded by
description: An Award is awarded by an Organization -- the original source of the funding, which may differ from the organization that administers it.

subject: award
label: is awarded to
description: An Award is awarded to an Organization -- the ultimate recipient, which may differ from the organization managing compliance on its behalf.

subject: award
label: is administered by
description: An Award may be administered day-to-day by an Organization other than the one that awarded or received it, such as a fiscal sponsor or intermediary.

subject: application
label: undergoes
description: An Application undergoes Review by one or more Reviewers.

subject: review
label: is conducted by
description: A Review is conducted by one or more Reviewers.

subject: review
label: is evaluated against
description: A Review evaluates an Application against published Review Criteria.

subject: review
label: may include
description: A Review may include a Site Visit before a Decision is made.

subject: review
label: produces
description: A Review produces a Decision.

subject: decision
label: results in
description: An approved Decision results in an Award.

subject: award
label: is formalized by
description: An Award is formalized by a Grant Agreement.

subject: grant-agreement
label: specifies
description: A Grant Agreement specifies Terms and Conditions, including whether funding is restricted or unrestricted.

subject: grant-agreement
label: may include
description: A Grant Agreement may include a Matching Requirement.

subject: grant-agreement
label: may specify
description: A Grant Agreement's Terms and Conditions may classify the award as Restricted Funding.

subject: grant-agreement
label: may specify
description: A Grant Agreement's Terms and Conditions may classify the award as Unrestricted Funding.

subject: award
label: has
description: An Award's funds are released according to a Payment Schedule.

subject: payment-schedule
label: is broken into
description: A Payment Schedule is broken into Installments.

subject: installment
label: may have
description: An Installment may carry a Payment Condition that must be met before it is disbursed.

subject: installment
label: is disbursed as
description: An Installment is disbursed as a Payment once any Payment Condition is satisfied.

subject: grantee
label: may request
description: Over the life of an Award, the Grantee may request a Budget Modification.

subject: amendment
label: modifies
description: An Amendment changes the Grant Agreement going forward; it does not retroactively alter Payments or Reports already completed under the prior terms.

subject: grant-agreement
label: attaches
description: A Grant Agreement attaches Compliance Requirements, including a Reporting Schedule.

subject: compliance-requirement
label: applies to
description: A Compliance Requirement applies to a specific Award -- distinct from the Grant Agreement specifying it: the Agreement is the document that spells out the requirement, while this relationship tracks which Award it actually binds. The same organization can be in good standing on one award and delinquent on another, so the requirement must attach to the Award, not the Grantee in the abstract.

subject: compliance-requirement
label: includes
description: A Compliance Requirement includes a Reporting Schedule that obligates the Grantee to submit Reports.

subject: compliance-requirement
label: may include
description: A Compliance Requirement may include an Audit.

subject: reporting-schedule
label: obligates
description: A Reporting Schedule obligates the Grantee to submit Reports on a defined cadence.

subject: report
label: is assessed against
description: Reports are assessed against the project's Logic Model in terms of Outputs and Outcomes.

subject: report
label: is assessed against
description: Reports are assessed against the project's Theory of Change in terms of Outputs and Outcomes.

subject: evaluation
label: assesses
description: An Evaluation assesses whether a grant-funded project achieved its intended Outputs.

subject: evaluation
label: assesses
description: An Evaluation assesses whether a grant-funded project achieved its intended Outcomes.

subject: award
label: reaches
description: Once all Payments are disbursed and all Compliance Requirements are satisfied, the Award reaches Closeout.

subject: award
label: follows
description: An Award's progression from decision through closeout follows the Grant Lifecycle sequence.

subject: program-officer
label: is associated with
description: A Program Officer is associated with one or more Grant Programs and typically owns the Review and monitoring relationship for Awards made under them.

subject: grant-administrator
label: is responsible for
description: A Grant Administrator is typically responsible for Report submission.

subject: grant-administrator
label: is responsible for
description: A Grant Administrator is typically responsible for tracking Compliance Requirements.

subject: fiscal-sponsorship-arrangement
label: supports
description: A Fiscal Sponsorship Arrangement supports a specific Sponsored Project carried out under the fiscal sponsor's umbrella.

subject: sponsored-project
label: is fiscally sponsored by
description: A Sponsored Project is fiscally sponsored by an Organization that provides the legal and administrative infrastructure it lacks on its own.

subject: donor-advisor
label: advises
description: A Donor Advisor advises a specific Donor-Advised Fund, holding non-binding privileges to recommend its grants and investments.

subject: donor-advisor
label: makes
description: A Donor Advisor makes a Grant Recommendation requesting that their Donor-Advised Fund make an award.

subject: grant-recommendation
label: recommends
description: A Grant Recommendation recommends a specific Organization as the award's recipient.

subject: grant-recommendation
label: concerns
description: A Grant Recommendation concerns a specific Fund -- ordinarily a Donor-Advised Fund -- that would pay for the recommended award.

subject: grant-recommendation
label: leads to
description: A Grant Recommendation the sponsoring organization accepts leads to an Award, mirroring how a Decision results in an Award in the direct-grant path.

subject: donor-advised-fund-arrangement
label: governs
description: A Donor-Advised Fund Arrangement governs the specific Donor-Advised Fund it establishes the advisory relationship for.

subject: collaborative-fund-arrangement
label: pools
description: A Collaborative Fund Arrangement pools multiple funders' contributions into a shared Fund.

subject: regranting-arrangement
label: regrants to
description: A Regranting Arrangement regrants funds to a downstream Organization, distinct from the Organization that supplied the funds originally.

subject: person
label: plays
description: A Person plays one or more Person Roles, each a contextual, independently-scoped occupancy rather than a permanent trait -- mirroring how an Organization plays Organization Roles (rel-organization-plays-role). A distinct predicate rather than a shared `playsRole` because the generator requires every relationship predicate to be globally unique (one fixed subject/object concept pair each); broadening `playsRole` into a real Person-or-Organization union predicate is a generator change deferred to when it's actually needed.

subject: person
label: is affiliated with
description: A Person is affiliated with an Organization, independent of which specific Person Role(s) they occupy there.

subject: person-role
label: applies within
description: A Person Role is scoped to the Organization it was granted within. This is the minimal case needed to make Person Role usable; broadening it to Award, Application, Agreement, and other contexts (matching how Organization Role's own context is broadened) is Phase 3.7 Milestone 2's job -- which will also need to resolve the same predicate-uniqueness constraint noted on personPlaysRole above, likely by generalizing the generator to support a shared predicate across a union of object concepts.

subject: application
label: proposes
description: An Application proposes the Project it is requesting funding for. The Application is the request; the Project is the work being proposed.

subject: award
label: funds
description: An Award commits funding to a Project. The Award is the funding commitment; the Project is the work performed using it.

subject: organization
label: implements
description: An Organization carries out a Project -- typically the Grantee, but modeled directly on Organization rather than a specific role so any organization implementing work (e.g. a Sponsored Project's Fiscal Sponsor) can be represented the same way.

subject: project
label: addresses
description: A Project addresses one or more identified Needs.

subject: need
label: is experienced by
description: A Need is experienced by a specific Population.

subject: project
label: serves
description: A Project serves a specific Population, which may or may not be the same Population that experiences the Need it addresses (e.g. a project can serve service providers on behalf of an affected population).

subject: project
label: takes place in
description: A Project operates within a Geographic Area. Distinct from any organization's registered address -- a project's operating area is not assumed to equal its implementing organization's or grant recipient's mailing address.

subject: project
label: uses
description: A Project uses Inputs (financial, human, material, or informational resources) to carry out its Activities.

subject: project
label: performs
description: A Project performs one or more Activities.

subject: activity
label: produces
description: An Activity produces one or more Outputs.

subject: output
label: contributes to
description: An Output contributes to an intended or observed Outcome. Deliberately "contributes to," not "causes" -- see Evidence Claim for how a specific causal or contributory interpretation of that contribution is represented and evidenced.

subject: outcome
label: contributes to
description: An Outcome contributes to a broader or longer-term Impact. Deliberately "contributes to," not "causes" -- see Evidence Claim for how a specific causal or contributory interpretation of that contribution is represented and evidenced.

subject: project
label: has
description: A Project has a Theory of Change articulating how its activities are expected to lead to desired long-term change.

subject: project
label: has
description: A Project has a Logic Model connecting its inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes.

subject: logic-model
label: includes
description: A Logic Model includes the Inputs it plans for.

subject: logic-model
label: includes
description: A Logic Model includes the Activities it plans for.

subject: logic-model
label: includes
description: A Logic Model includes the Outputs it plans for.

subject: logic-model
label: includes
description: A Logic Model includes the Outcomes it plans for.

subject: result
label: is measured by
description: A Result (Output, Outcome, or Impact) is measured by an Indicator. Declared against the abstract Result concept rather than each subtype separately, so any Output, Outcome, or Impact instance can be measured the same way.

subject: indicator
label: has
description: An Indicator has a Target -- the planned value expected by a defined date.

subject: indicator
label: has
description: An Indicator has one or more Measurements -- the observed values recorded over time. Never equated with the Indicator's Target: a Target is planned, a Measurement is observed.

subject: measurement
label: was observed for
description: A Measurement was observed for a specific Population.

subject: measurement
label: was observed in
description: A Measurement was observed in a specific Geographic Area.

subject: evaluation
label: evaluates
description: An Evaluation assesses a Project.

subject: evaluation
label: produces
description: An Evaluation produces one or more Evidence Claims.

subject: evidence-claim
label: is about
description: An Evidence Claim is about a Result. Declared against the abstract Result concept rather than each subtype separately, so a claim can concern any Output, Outcome, or Impact instance.

subject: evidence-claim
label: is supported by
description: An Evidence Claim is supported by one or more pieces of Evidence.

subject: report
label: provides
description: A Report can itself serve as Evidence supporting an Evidence Claim (e.g. the administrative data or narrative it contains).

subject: agent
label: plays
description: An Agent (Person or Organization) plays one or more Roles. The preferred predicate for new data now that Agent exists as a shared superclass, replacing the separate playsRole (Organization) and personPlaysRole (Person) predicates -- both kept and still valid on existing data, not migrated, per this project's policy of never deleting or force-migrating published predicates.

subject: grant-agreement
label: specifies
description: A Grant Agreement specifies one or more Grant Terms. Declared against the abstract Grant Term concept rather than each subtype separately, so any Use Restriction, Grant Condition, Approval Requirement, Reporting Requirement, Compliance Requirement, or Reporting Schedule instance satisfies it the same way.

subject: grant-term
label: applies to
description: A Grant Term applies to a specific Award. Declared against the abstract Grant Term concept, used by Use Restriction, Grant Condition, Approval Requirement, and Reporting Requirement instances -- Compliance Requirement keeps its own existing, more specific appliesToAward predicate unchanged, and Matching Requirement/Payment Condition/Reporting Schedule are already reachable from Award through their existing relationships, so none of those three need this one too.

subject: grant-condition
label: has responsible party
description: A Grant Condition optionally identifies the Agent (Person or Organization) responsible for satisfying it -- e.g. the grantee organization for a matching requirement, or a fiscal sponsor rather than the project itself.

subject: approval-requirement
label: requires approval from
description: An Approval Requirement identifies the Agent whose authorization is required before the governed change, expenditure, action, or deviation may occur -- typically the Funder.

subject: reporting-requirement
label: is fulfilled by
description: A Reporting Requirement is fulfilled by a submitted Report. Requirement is what must be supplied; Report is the artifact that was actually supplied.

subject: award
label: has classification
description: An Award has one or more Classification Assignments (e.g. Candid PCS Subjects) drawn from an external or internal classification scheme. The scheme classifies the Award; it does not redefine it.

subject: population
label: has classification
description: A Population has one or more Classification Assignments (e.g. Candid PCS Populations) describing its characteristics. Multiple classifications are valid, since a population may have several characteristics at once; the Population resource itself represents the actual contextual group, not a combination of taxonomy terms.

subject: indirect-cost-rate
label: applies to
description: An Indirect Cost Rate applies to a specific Award -- the rate itself may be negotiated at the organization level (independent of any one award), but this relationship tracks which Award's budget it is actually being charged against, mirroring why Compliance Requirement's own appliesToAward attaches to a specific Award rather than the Grantee in the abstract: the same organization can have a different applicable rate situation on one award than another. A distinct predicate from Compliance Requirement's own appliesToAward for the same reason every relationship predicate in this ontology is unique -- the generator requires one fixed declared subject per predicate.
